description: morgen is an open-source MATLAB and Octave test platform for comparing models, solvers and model order reduction methods for gas networks and other energy network systems based on the isothermal Euler equations. It was written by Christian Himpe and Sara Grundel, with the companion paper by Himpe, Grundel and Benner, to support research on fast transient simulation of gas transport networks. The method is location-independent; networks, scenarios, models, solvers and reductors are modular and can be extended from templates, and scripts reproduce the experiments of three papers. It runs in MATLAB 2020b or later or GNU Octave 6.1 or later, with the emgr library included, and the current version 1.2 (October 2022) is archived on Zenodo. It is licensed under BSD-2-Clause at no cost. Caveats: it is described as research software, the last commit dates from May 2023, and it needs MATLAB or Octave. Simulation uses are transient gas network flow simulation and building reduced models for control or optimisation. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
